hints: Remember that a reducing agent works by being oxidised itself, so look for an oxide where the element can still increase its oxidation number.
Work out the oxidation state in each common oxide: $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$, $\text{MgO}$ and $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ all contain the metal at its maximum group oxidation state.
Compare that with sulfur burning to $\text{SO}_2$ where sulfur is only +4 and can still be oxidised up to +6, so decide which oxide can donate electrons.
walkthrough:
**What makes an oxide a reducing agent?**

A reducing agent reduces another species by donating electrons to it. That means the reducing agent itself is oxidised, so its central atom must be able to increase its oxidation number further.

Rule to use:
$$\text{reducing agent is oxidised: oxidation number increases}$$

**Check the metal oxides from Na, Mg and Al**

These metals burn to form very stable ionic oxides where the metal is already at its highest possible oxidation state.

$$4\text{Na} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{Na}_2\text{O}$$
$$2\text{Mg} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{MgO}$$
$$4\text{Al} + 3\text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$$
In $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$, Na is +1. In $\text{MgO}$, Mg is +2. In $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$, Al is +3. None can be oxidised further, so none can act as a reducing agent.

**Check sulfur burning in oxygen**

Sulfur burns with a blue flame to form sulfur dioxide, a covalent molecular oxide.

$$\text{S} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{SO}_2$$
In $\text{SO}_2$, oxygen is -2, so sulfur is +4. But sulfur is in Group 16 and its maximum oxidation state is +6, as in $\text{SO}_3$ and $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$.

**Conclude which oxide can reduce**

Because +4 can still increase to +6, $\text{SO}_2$ can be oxidised and therefore can donate electrons to another species. That is exactly what a reducing agent does, for example when $\text{SO}_2$ reduces acidified dichromate(VI) or decolourises bromine water.

options.A: Incorrect. Sodium burns to $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$ where Na is +1, its maximum oxidation state. It cannot be oxidised further, so it cannot act as a reducing agent.
options.B: Incorrect. Magnesium burns to $\text{MgO}$ where Mg is +2, its maximum oxidation state. $\text{MgO}$ is a stable basic oxide with no electrons to donate by oxidation.
options.C: Incorrect. Aluminium burns to $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ where Al is +3, its maximum oxidation state. This oxide is amphoteric but is neither oxidised nor reduced easily.
options.D: Correct. Sulfur burns to $\text{SO}_2$ where S is +4. Since sulfur can be oxidised further to +6 in $\text{SO}_3$ or sulfate, $\text{SO}_2$ is a good reducing agent.
